name: Genre-specific sound and MIDI micro packs (acid, EBM, dark disco, industrial)
pain: Producers want small, focused packs for niche dark club sounds: acid lines with MIDI patterns, EBM bass racks, aggrotech snares, EBM/witch-house drums. Generic packs and tutorials don't cover these sounds. Version mismatches make some free presets unusable.
who_pays: Bedroom and semi-pro techno/EBM/acid producers using Vital, Serum or Ableton stock devices
pay_signal: Explicit 'I'd buy that' for a micro pack of acid Serum presets plus MIDI patterns (496). EBM racks are already sold with discount codes (524). People pay for Phoscyon and regret missing sales (520).
product_idea: Build it: an 'Inch of Shadow' series of small packs for Ableton stock racks and Vital/Serum. Examples: EBM bass + sequence MIDI, acid 303 lines + MIDI, dark disco drums, industrial snares. Each pack is version-tagged so it loads in current releases. Use it: his own studio patches become the source material.
known_competitors: Studio Brootle EBM racks, Zenhiser/Loopmasters genre packs, tutorial-channel freebies, Phoscyon/TS404 factory patterns
check_next: Search Splice and Loopmasters for 'EBM' and 'dark disco' pack counts and prices. Post one free pack to r/TechnoProduction and r/synthesizers to measure downloads.

crowding.reason: Acid Serum+MIDI and Ableton EBM racks are already sold by many vendors at $15-$25 with Serum 2/Live-version compatibility stated; only Vital and aggrotech/witch-house niches remain unchecked.

name: Seamless song and set transitions in live hybrid/hardware sets
pain: Performers get silence or dropouts when loading the next Ableton set or switching hardware projects (Eloquencer, Octatrack, Tonverk). They build fragile chains of loopers, reset clocks and MIDI macros to avoid gaps.
who_pays: Live electronic performers using Ableton plus hardware
pay_signal: Users buy extra hardware (a 404 looper, an MC8 MIDI controller, a Drumbrute) purely as transition workarounds (133, 165). They run expensive rigs (Push, UAD Apollo) and still lack a solution (32).
product_idea: Build it: a Max for Live 'bridge' device that records the last N bars of the master or chosen tracks. It loops them, quantized to the beat, while the next set or project loads, then crossfades out on the downbeat. A companion standalone helper could keep audio running across Ableton set loads. Use it in his own live sets.
known_competitors: Hardware loopers (SP-404, Boss RC), the giant-single-set approach, Eloquencer reset tricks; no dedicated transition tool found
check_next: Prototype whether a Max for Live device keeps audio playing during an Ableton set load; it likely doesn't, so a standalone helper may be needed. Ask r/ableton live performers whether they would pay €15–25.

crowding.reason: No dedicated tool keeps audio and clock running across Ableton set or hardware project loads; AbleSet's multi-file mode still leaves a 10-15s load gap, and synced loopers fail because clock stops, while users pay $129-$299 for nearby setlist tools.

name: MIDI clock sync and jitter diagnostics
pain: Clock drift, arpeggiators that ignore external clock, sequencers that don't reset, and off-grid retriggers break hardware jams and multitrack recording. Users can't tell which device is at fault.
who_pays: Hardware techno producers who multitrack into a DAW, and iOS host users
pay_signal: One user is buying an E-RM Multiclock plus an MRCC MIDI router to fix sync, calling jitter a dealbreaker (95). There are 2-star reviews of paid apps over sync (207, 239). Owners of expensive synths are pushing vendors for fixes (69).
product_idea: Build it: a web MIDI or Max for Live 'sync doctor'. It measures incoming clock jitter and drift per device and checks start/stop/reset behaviour. It records audio onsets against the grid and outputs a per-device report, with recommended offsets for Ableton track delay. Use it to tune his own rig.
known_competitors: E-RM Multiclock, Innerclock Sync Gen, MIDI monitors (MIDI-OX, Snoize); no consumer jitter/latency analyzer found
check_next: Test whether Web MIDI timestamps are precise enough, or whether audio-onset measurement is required. Check the Elektronauts and Gearspace sync threads for demand.

crowding.reason: Paid sync fixers are crowded ($10-$600) but every jitter/latency diagnostic tool found is free and one open-source 'MIDI Sync Doctor' already does much of the idea; no proof anyone pays for diagnosis alone.

name: Elektron pattern, kit and song-mode management tool
pain: Sound edits don't propagate across patterns. Building song mode in a merged live project means re-entering everything by hand. Sample folders can't be synced cleanly. Users already turn to firmware mods and community tools.
who_pays: Digitakt II, Digitone II and Octatrack owners writing full tracks or live sets
pay_signal: Owners of €1000+ boxes use elk-herd and firmware mods to work around gaps (124, 111, 414). One commenter notes Claude could build firmware features (407). There is a recurring 'I would like a solution' sentiment (478).
product_idea: Build it: a desktop/web companion that reads Elektron project data via SysEx/backup files. It would propagate a kit change to all patterns, copy song-mode chains between projects, and diff/sync sample folders. Use it only if he works on Elektron boxes.
known_competitors: elk-herd, Elektron Transfer, community firmware mods
check_next: Check how much of the Digitakt II/Digitone II SysEx and project format elk-herd already decodes, and whether its license allows building on it. Ask on Elektronauts which feature is most wanted.

crowding.reason: Free community tools (elk-herd for Digitakt and Digitakt II, Octatrack Manager and ot-tools for Octatrack) plus the free official Elektron Transfer already cover project, pattern and sample management; the only paid proof is old OctaEdit at $75, with current status unverified.

name: Sample prep for hardware samplers (pre-stretch, slice, batch format)
pain: Tonverk has no time-stretch. Digitakt slicing has structural limits. Sample sync and folder management are clumsy. Getting loops in at the right BPM and slice layout is manual, and on iOS uploads aren't even possible.
who_pays: Owners of Tonverk, Digitakt, Octatrack, Model:Samples/Cycles and 404 samplers
pay_signal: Users buy extra samplers just for stretching and slicing (74, 131). One user built a free uploader because no tool existed (116). A user nearly returned an Octatrack over clicks caused by sample edges (128).
product_idea: Build it: a web tool (WebAudio plus a stretch library) that batch time-stretches loops to a target BPM and auto-slices to N equal or transient slices with Elektron-friendly limits. It would add zero-crossing fades against clicks, normalize, and export naming and folder structure per device. Use it for his own hardware sampling.
known_competitors: Elektron Transfer, OctaChainer, DAW manual export, Ableton warping
check_next: Search 'OctaChainer' and 'Tonverk time stretch' threads for unmet features. Test the quality of open-source stretchers (Rubber Band licence, signalsmith-stretch).

crowding.reason: Free tools (DigiChain, OctaChainer 2, elektron-sample-prep, Elektron Transfer) already cover chaining, slicing, device formatting and upload; only pitch-preserving batch stretch to BPM looks open, and there's no proof people pay for that alone.

name: Hardware/Overbridge multitrack capture templates
pain: Overbridge multitracks skip master compressor, panning and FX buses. Arp parameters can't be automated. Routing pedals as aux sends from boxes is unclear. Users struggle to recreate the hardware mix in the DAW.
who_pays: Elektron and hardware users recording jams into Ableton, Logic or Pro Tools
pay_signal: These users have already paid for Analog Rytm, Digitakt II and Outbox 8 hardware. They call the gaps disappointing and search for workarounds (125, 140, 113).
product_idea: Both: use Ableton's new 32-output Overbridge support. Build and sell Ableton templates or racks per Elektron box that rebuild master comp, panning and FX returns. Add a Max for Live device that records knob moves for non-automatable parameters as clip automation.
known_competitors: Overbridge itself, YouTuber templates (ezbot Octatrack templates), manual routing
check_next: Confirm which Elektron master FX can be emulated closely with stock Ableton devices. Check Gumroad and Patreon for existing Overbridge template sales.

crowding.reason: Only free forum templates, one $2+ pay-what-you-want Digitakt template and a Patreon post exist, none rebuilds the master compressor or effects returns, and Elektron owners do pay for templates ($18 EZBOT), though the price ceiling looks low and the Max for Live recorder was not checked.

name: Voice/LLM control of Ableton
pain: Users want to operate Live by talking to it: loading devices, edits, technical questions. Stream Deck macros are a clunky substitute, and blind or one-handed users are especially blocked.
who_pays: Ableton users, accessibility users, Stream Deck users
pay_signal: Repeated 'please release it' and 'I'd love to try it', and one user wants to buy one as a gift (591). People already pay for Stream Deck workflows they want to replace (587, 51). One comment asks about token costs, showing they expect a paid service (593).
product_idea: Build it: a Max for Live device plus a local bridge to Claude (or similar) via the Live API. It would load devices by name, rename and colour tracks, set routing, and answer 'how do I' questions. Accessibility mode would read the state back. He already directs Claude Code, so this fits his skills; use it in his own sessions.
known_competitors: Open-source AbletonMCP, the unreleased device shown in the video, Stream Deck Ableton plugins
check_next: Install AbletonMCP to see how far it already goes. Check whether the device in the video has launched and at what price.

crowding.reason: 4+ paid voice/chat Ableton assistants (VIXSOUND, LIA, Tine, StudioPilot) plus free open-source Max for Live/MCP bridges (Producer Pal, AbletonMCP) already do this, and the video device (Melosurf) now has a product site.

who_pays: Ableton users with large paid plugin libraries

product_idea: Build it: a small standalone app that scans VST3/AU preset folders and indexes them by plugin and tags. It would audition presets and drop them into Live as .adv/.vstpreset via drag-out or a Max for Live loader. Use it for his own plugin library.

name: Missing MIDI generators and transforms for Ableton
pain: Users want chords typed as text turned into MIDI, sequences with probability-weighted note lengths, beat-based LFO sync in odd meters, MPE curves drawn on notes, and true linear fades. These all currently need manual drawing or are blocked by API limits.
who_pays: Ableton Suite users who buy Max for Live devices
pay_signal: Users upgrade to Suite and buy Max for Live devices to fill gaps (551, 558), and some developers sell device packs. Requests are concrete and repeated, and one user lists exact missing features (548).
product_idea: Build it: a bundle of small Live 12 MIDI Tools / Max for Live devices: chord-text-to-MIDI, a weighted note-length and rhythm generator that evolves over time, and a meter-aware LFO. Sell it as a cheap pack on Gumroad or maxforlive.com. Use it for writing dark wave basslines and arps.
known_competitors: Free maxforlive.com devices, Sting 2, CHORDimist, Live 12 built-in MIDI Generators
check_next: Search maxforlive.com for 'chord text' and 'note length probability' to see what already exists. Note the Live API's MPE limits (23) before promising MPE drawing.

crowding.reason: Chord-text-to-MIDI (M2TM Chords, €15) and probability/note-length generators (Manifest Audio MIDI Tools, Live 12 built-ins) already exist as paid and free tools; only the meter-aware LFO, MPE and fade pains remain unverified niches.

name: Live performance FX overview and momentary control in Ableton
pain: Performers can't see a whole FX chain or several tracks at once. Momentary effects, instant reverb kill, mapping sends on controllers and immediate-but-quantized clip launches all need fiddly rack and MIDI-map workarounds.
who_pays: Ableton live performers using Push, Move or other MIDI controllers
pay_signal: Owners of Push, Move and Keylab controllers are hunting for third-party devices (4: 'some kind of Max for Live device or 3rd party software'). People already pay for the controllers but get stuck on the workflow.
product_idea: Build it: a Max for Live 'performance panel' device. It shows the key parameters of the chosen tracks on one screen, offers momentary/latch FX slots with a one-button tail kill, and supports MIDI learn for sends. Use it in his own live sets alongside the transition bridge.
known_competitors: Clyphx Pro, Isotonik devices, custom Drum Rack momentary setups, Push/Move native mappings
check_next: Check ClyphX Pro's feature list and price for overlap. Interview 3–5 r/ableton live users about their must-have controls.

crowding.reason: Momentary FX is already solved by cheap/free tools (built-in Live features, Push Momentary FX, ClyphX Pro) and people pay £16-£66 for Ableton control devices, but search ran out before confirming whether a combined multi-track overview + tail-kill panel already exists.
